text:
Anton Frondell is 19, the third pick of the 2025 draft, and Chicago has given him a job most rookies never see: the shutdown center role, as The Athletic's Scott Powers has written. He has 10 points in 20 games, and the role shows in the numbers more than the points do.

At five-on-five the Blackhawks get just 35.5% of the expected goals with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), 7.5 points worse than without him. Faceoffs are part of it. Chicago is last in the league in faceoffs, Powers noted, and he had Frondell at 2 of 13 in a loss to Winnipeg. His own finishing is fine: 4 goals on 4.0 expected.

The tools are visible. His hardest shot, 94.2 mph, is in the 98th percentile among forwards, and he scored twice against Boston on a nine-shot night. Forwards picked in the top five usually reach 200 NHL games, and the closest comparisons, Beckett Sennecke, Adam Fantilli, Logan Cooley and Mason McTavish, put up 0.54 to 0.73 points a game in their first full seasons. Watch the faceoff circle and his on-ice chances against; that's where his season is being decided.
headline: Frondell is learning the hard minutes
